title: Rational restriction comparisons and mixed scalar squares
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, and a fixed algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-pur-conventions]. Let $f:Y\to X$ be a morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], using the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For every finite intermediate field $E\subset\Omega$, put $\mathcal C_E(W)=D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$ for $W=X,Y$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], and use the integral pullback $r_E=Lf^*$, completed tensor and coefficient unit $\mathbf1_{E,W}=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$ [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Assume these operations take values in the displayed constructible categories and that $r_E$ is $\mathcal O_E$-linear. Write $S^W_{L/E}$ for integral scalar extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. Let
$$b_{L/E,K}:S^Y_{L/E}(r_EK)\xrightarrow{\sim}r_L(S^X_{L/E}K),\qquad
\theta^W_{L/E,M,N}:S^W_{L/E}(M\widehat\otimes N)\xrightarrow{\sim}S^W_{L/E}M\widehat\otimes S^W_{L/E}N$$
be exactly the canonical comparisons of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], with their identity and tower comparisons [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition]. Suppose given natural integral isomorphisms $\mu_{E,M,N}:r_E(M\widehat\otimes N)\xrightarrow{\sim}r_EM\widehat\otimes r_EN$, $\epsilon_E:r_E\mathbf1_{E,X}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf1_{E,Y}$, and the canonical coefficient scalar-unit isomorphisms $\upsilon^W_{L/E}:S^W_{L/E}\mathbf1_{E,W}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf1_{L,W}$ of [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible]. Assume the mixed squares
$$(b_{L/E,M}\widehat\otimes b_{L/E,N})\circ\theta^Y_{L/E,r_EM,r_EN}\circ S^Y_{L/E}(\mu_{E,M,N})
=\mu_{L,S^X_{L/E}M,S^X_{L/E}N}\circ r_L(\theta^X_{L/E,M,N})\circ b_{L/E,M\widehat\otimes N},$$
$$\upsilon^Y_{L/E}\circ S^Y_{L/E}(\epsilon_E)=\epsilon_L\circ r_L(\upsilon^X_{L/E})\circ b_{L/E,\mathbf1_{E,X}}$$
hold integrally.

In the raw rationalizations $D^b_c(W,E)$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], the components $\mu_E\otimes1$, $\epsilon_E\otimes1$, $b_{L/E}\otimes1$, $\theta^W_{L/E}\otimes1$ and $\upsilon^W_{L/E}\otimes1$ are natural isomorphisms for the rational operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. The rational $b$ and $\theta$ have the same identity and tower compatibilities, and both displayed mixed squares hold rationally. The pullback and tensor actions on pure arrows are $r_E(u\otimes a)=r_E(u)\otimes a$ and $(u\otimes a)\otimes_E^L(v\otimes c)=(u\widehat\otimes^L v)\otimes ac$; these formulas respect balancing and extend additively, with the localized integral inverse comparisons as inverses. Every specified integral equation between these comparisons, identities and composites remains an equation after rationalization.

proof.text: Write $Q_{E,W}(u)=u\otimes1$. The raw localization has the same objects and composition $(u\otimes a)\circ(v\otimes c)=(u\circ v)\otimes ac$, so $Q$ preserves identities, compositions and equality. Integral representatives therefore suffice for objects, including the coefficient unit; there are no extra idempotent objects to treat. In the following calculations all scalar products are taken in the target coefficient field.

proof.text: Use rationalDerivedPullback_existsUnique and sfRationalScalarExtension_existsUnique, whose uniquely chosen functors are the published rational operations. Their object formulas preserve the integral representative, and their pure-arrow formulas give the pullback and coefficient-extension actions directly. At coefficient one these formulas say that unary whiskering commutes with the localization functor Q. No separate construction by semilinear localization is needed.

source.place: Final paragraph: rationalization for E; explicit raw-Hom calculation in this split (agent).

proof.text: The rational tensor operation is the separately linear extension specified in the rational-level clause of the operation definition. Explicitly put $T(u\otimes a,v\otimes c)=(u\widehat\otimes^L v)\otimes ac$. For $s\in\mathcal O_E$, replacing $(su)\otimes a$ by $u\otimes sa$ leaves this value unchanged, since $(su)\widehat\otimes v=s(u\widehat\otimes v)$; the identical calculation in the other variable gives $sac=asc$. Additivity in $u,a,v,c$ then respects all tensor-product relations and defines the claimed action on finite sums. On pure arrows the bifunctor composition law has coefficient $(aa')(cc')=(ac)(a'c')$, and the integral bifunctor law supplies the integral arrow; identities have coefficient $1$. Distributing finite sums proves the same laws on all arrows. In particular $T(Q(u),Q(v))=Q(u\widehat\otimes^L v)$.

source.place: Final paragraph: rationalization for E; explicit raw-Hom calculation in this split (agent).

proof.text: The existence-and-uniqueness specifications of rationalPullbackScalarComparison, rationalTensorScalarComparison and constantCoefficientRationalScalarIso prescribe precisely the localized integral hom components. Their object formulas identify both endpoints. Since Q carries the corresponding integral isomorphism to an isomorphism, equality of hom components identifies the isomorphism, and hence also its inverse component. The supplied unit comparison is transported across the pullback object equality from Q of the given integral isomorphism. This argument applies to identity and ramified coefficient extensions and needs no injectivity of integral Homs.

source.place: Final paragraph: rationalization for E; explicit raw-Hom calculation in this split (agent).

proof.text: Apply the proved generic rawBilinearIso_existsUnique theorem from DerivedPullbackTensorHom to U = integral tensor followed by integral pullback and V = the product of the two integral pullbacks followed by integral tensor, with comparison μ. The object equations are tensor_obj and pullback_obj. For U, postcompose the tensor bilinear map with the additive rational pullback map; for V, precompose the tensor bilinear map with the two additive pullback maps. The pure-arrow formulas identify both actions with the scalar product times the integral action. The generic theorem proves naturality by tensor induction in both arrows and localizes the integral inverse equations. Its component normalization fixes hom components; iso_inv_heq identifies the inverse components. Uniqueness follows from extensionality of natural transformations and of isomorphisms. The canonical theta comparison already has its published normalized construction.

source.place: Final paragraph: rationalization for E; explicit raw-Hom calculation in this split (agent).

proof.text: Fix $M,N$ in $\mathcal C_E(X)$, which also represent every rational object. Apply $Q_{L,Y}$ to the assumed integral tensor mixed-square equality. Steps 2-3 identify its left side with $(\bar b_M\otimes_L\bar b_N)\circ\bar\theta^Y\circ\bar S^Y(\bar\mu_E)$, and its right side with $\bar\mu_L\circ\bar r_L(\bar\theta^X)\circ\bar b_{M\widehat\otimes N}$: every comparison has coefficient $1$, and both functor action and tensor action commute with $Q$. Applying the same $Q_{L,Y}$ to the assumed unit equality gives $\bar\upsilon^Y\circ\bar S^Y(\bar\epsilon_E)=\bar\epsilon_L\circ\bar r_L(\bar\upsilon^X)\circ\bar b_{\mathbf1}$. Sources and targets agree because raw localization preserves objects. These componentwise equations are equations of natural transformations by steps 4-5.

source.place: Final paragraph: rationalization for E; explicit raw-Hom calculation in this split (agent).

proof.text: First identify sfIntegralOrdinaryComparison with the natural isomorphism whose components are scalarCompletionIso: both have the same chain-level normalization, so uniqueness identifies them. The integral scalar unitor is inverse completion comparison followed by the ordinary scalar unitor. The integral associator is inverse completion at the outer extension, ordinary scalar applied to inverse completion at the inner extension, the ordinary associator, and completion for the composite extension. Naturality of scalarCompletion conjugates every completed scalar map to the ordinary scalar map. Expand scalarPullbackCompleted and scalarTensorCompleted, cancel the completion isomorphisms, and apply ordinary-operation naturality and scalarOperationsOrdinary_unit or scalarOperationsOrdinary_tower. This proves the integral identity and tower equations for the specified comparisons. Now use the published rational unitor/associator component specifications and the pure-arrow formulas at coefficient one. Applying Q to each integral equation gives the required rational equation, with unchanged chosen comparisons and no cancellation of integral Homs.

source.place: Final paragraph: rationalization for E; explicit raw-Hom calculation in this split (agent).

proof.text: The equation calculus consists of functorial preservation of equality, identities and composition by Q, and the pullback, scalar and bilinear tensor pure-arrow formulas at coefficient one. Together with the proved comparison and inverse component formulas these evaluate every finite well-typed expression recursively. Thus both rational expressions in any specified integral equation are its Q-images, and applying Q proves their equality.
